content.value_statement: Bulk RNA-seq analysis requires careful count formatting, design formulas, and adjusted p-value interpretation. This skill guides PyDESeq2 workflows from input validation through statistics, exports, and plots.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading counts and metadata into the samples by genes format required by PyDESeq2.
Explains single-factor and multi-factor design formulas for differential expression analysis.
Shows how to run DeseqDataSet and DeseqStats workflows with contrasts and Wald tests.
Covers FDR-adjusted p-values, log fold change shrinkage, and result interpretation.
Provides script guidance for CSV exports, pickle outputs, volcano plots, and MA plots.
Helps troubleshoot sample-index mismatches, full-rank design errors, and no-significant-gene results.
limitations: Focused on bulk RNA-seq differential expression, not specialized single-cell methods.
Requires count data and metadata with matching sample identifiers.
Does not replace statistical review of experimental design or biological interpretation.
Requires PyDESeq2 and optional plotting packages to run workflows locally.

use_cases.title: Compare treatment groups
use_cases.description: Run a treated versus control analysis and identify genes with significant adjusted p-values.

use_cases.title: Plan a batch-aware model
use_cases.description: Build a design formula that controls for batch or covariates before testing the condition of interest.

use_cases.title: Automate standard outputs
use_cases.description: Use the included script guidance to produce result tables, significant-gene lists, and diagnostic plots.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me analyze counts.csv and metadata.csv with PyDESeq2 for treated versus control samples. Explain the required data format and outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Add batch adjustment
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a PyDESeq2 design that tests condition while controlling for batch. Review my metadata columns and suggest the contrast.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret result tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PyDESeq2 results table. Explain baseMean, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj, and how to select significant genes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a reusable workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable PyDESeq2 analysis workflow with filtering, model fitting, contrasts, LFC shrinkage, exports, and volcano and MA plots.

output_examples.input: A user asks for treated versus control analysis using count and metadata CSV files.
output_examples.output: The skill provides a PyDESeq2 workflow, explains data orientation, recommends the contrast, and lists expected result files.

output_examples.input: A user reports a design matrix full-rank error.
output_examples.output: The skill explains likely confounding, suggests checking condition by batch tables, and recommends model simplification or interaction terms.

output_examples.input: A user wants publication-ready differential expression summaries.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines FDR filtering, log fold change interpretation, significant gene summaries, and volcano and MA plot generation.

best_practices: Confirm count matrix orientation and matching sample identifiers before fitting the model.
Filter low-count genes and samples with missing metadata before statistical testing.
Report the design formula, contrast, adjusted p-value threshold, and shrinkage status with results.
anti_patterns: Using raw p-values as significance calls without false discovery rate correction.
Feeding normalized expression values when the workflow expects raw integer counts.
Ignoring batch effects or using confounded design variables without checking metadata.

faq.question: What data does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects a count matrix and metadata table with matching sample names.

faq.question: Can it handle batch effects?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains multi-factor designs that include batch before the main condition.

faq.question: Does it run the analysis automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide commands and scripts, but local execution depends on installed Python packages and user files.

faq.question: What outputs can it help create?
faq.answer: It supports result tables, significant-gene lists, saved analysis objects, volcano plots, and MA plots.

faq.question: Does it replace DESeq2 in R?
faq.answer: No. It helps use the Python PyDESeq2 implementation for similar bulk RNA-seq workflows.

faq.question: Can it interpret biological meaning?
faq.answer: It explains statistical results, but biological conclusions still require domain review and follow-up validation.
